name: 410. OpenAI image edit refuses the unified fields it cannot deliver; a streamed image response reports usage.output_images (openai image edit fields) [SERIAL]
description: TXE-6984 regression, contract C4 and C5. Local fixture regression, no live provider calls: run with providerErrorFixture=1 against the gateway of tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json, with tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs as the only upstream (see folder 331 for the fixture's OpenAI image paths). Every row names the key with x-bf-api-key and reads back from /__wire the requests that reached the fixture. Pinned: an image edit to openai or azure carrying aspect_ratio, resolution, type, upscale_factor or target_megapixels, which OpenAI's edit API has no field for in its multipart form or its JSON edit body, is answered 400 caller_unsupported_parameter with error.param naming the field and makes no upstream call, as a form, as JSON with link inputs, and with stream set (before, the field was dropped and the edit ran without it); the completed frame of a streamed generation or edit carries usage.output_images 1 next to OpenAI's token usage, with two previews in the stream, because partial_image_index numbers the previews of one image and is not an image count (before, a streamed response had no image count). Two rows pin the same count on azure, whose streams run on the same handlers and reach the fixture on /openai/v1/images/generations and /openai/v1/images/edits. Four rows enter by the OpenAI drop-in route (/openai/v1/images/edits, /openai/v1/images/generations), which has its own multipart parser and stream converter: the refusal for aspect_ratio and for upscale_factor (which that parser did not read before, so it never reached the check), and the count on both streams.

item.name: openai/gpt-image-1.5 /v1/images/generations stream with two previews: the completed frame carries usage.output_images 1 (openai image edit fields)

exec: pm.test('openai image edit fields setup: the fixture was reset', function () {
// wire: the requests that reached the fixture, bytes as they arrived.

function wire(cb) { pm.sendRequest({ url: FX + '/__wire', method: 'GET' }, function (err, res) { pm.test('the fixture answered /__wire', function () { pm.expect(err, String(err)).to.equal(null); pm.expect(res.code).to.equal(200); }); cb(res.json().data[0].calls); }); }

pm.test('the client gets 200 and a server-sent event stream', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code, pm.response.text()).to.equal(200); pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type'), JSON.stringify(pm.response.headers.toObject())).to.match(/^text\/event-stream/); });
var events = text.split('\n').filter(function (l) { return l.indexOf('data: {') === 0; }).map(function (l) { return JSON.parse(l.slice(6)); });

pm.test('the stream is 2 previews of one image, then the completed event', function () { pm.expect(events.map(function (e) { return e.type; }), text).to.deep.equal(['image_generation.partial_image', 'image_generation.partial_image', 'image_generation.completed']); });

pm.test('the completed frame carries usage.output_images 1: one finished image, whatever the number of previews', function () { pm.expect(last.usage, text).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(last.usage.output_images, text).to.equal(1); });

pm.test('OpenAI\'s token usage is kept next to the count', function () { pm.expect(last.usage.input_tokens, text).to.equal(12); pm.expect(last.usage.output_tokens, text).to.equal(272); pm.expect(last.usage.total_tokens, text).to.equal(284); });
pm.test('no preview frame carries usage', function () { events.slice(0, -1).forEach(function (e) { pm.expect(e.usage, JSON.stringify(e)).to.equal(undefined); }); });

wire(function (calls) { var images = imageCalls(calls); pm.test('exactly one upstream call, with stream set', function () { pm.expect(images, JSON.stringify(calls)).to.have.length(1); pm.expect(images[0].path).to.equal('/v1/images/generations'); pm.expect(images[0].contentType, JSON.stringify(images[0]).slice(0, 300)).to.match(/^application\/json/); pm.expect(images[0].body).to.match(/"stream":true|name="stream"\r\n\r\ntrue/); }); });
